title: Locale sanity eval prompt variants (CJK + RTL) - 2026
content:
Goal:
This prompt pack is a compact sanities-and-edgecases set for model onboarding and regression checks focused on locale-sensitive behaviours: CJK (zh-J, ja, ko), RTL (ar, he, fa), mixed bidi, and translation-normalization quirks (dates, numbers, currency, quotations, percent/thousand separators, ordinal/worded numbers). Aim is fast smoke/regression runs (200-2k prompts) that catch common degradations after model roll or quantization changes.

Scope / non-goals:
- Includes generation/translation + formatting canonicalization checks only.
- Not a full-blown human eval suite; metric thresholds are conservative and intended to flag regressions for deeper investigation.
- Does not attempt exhaustive dialect coverage (e.g., variants of Arabic across regions).

How to use:
- Run as part of onboarding job: seed=42, temperature=0.0 for deterministic models; temp=0.2 for stochastic comparisons.
- Compare current model vs baseline via exact-match, normalized-string-match, and fuzzy metrics (chrF, BLEU, token edit distance). Fail if >X% regression on any critical bucket (see regression matrix below).

Prompt design principles (notes/heuristics):
- Keep prompts short + context-limited to isolate locale formatting/translation behavior.
- Include "source language hint" and desired output canonicalization when relevant (e.g., "Return ISO date YYYY-MM-DD").
- Include both natural and artificially contrived edge cases (zero-width joiners, bidi markers, mixed-languages in one line).
- Include both surface form and semantic equivalence checks (e.g., currency conversion vs format-only).

Buckets & sample cases (representative examples) :
- CJK:
  * Dates: "2026年3月2日" -> canonicalize to "2026-03-02"
  * Numerics with ideographic separators: "1,234" vs "1 234" vs "1,234.56" in zh-Hant contexts
  * Width variants: "１月" (full-width) -> map to "1月" or ISO where requested
  * Japanese honorifics & spacing: "田中さん, 2026年3月" -> keep honorifics intact when translating to English unless asked
  * CJK punctuation: handle full-width comma/period (、。) vs ASCII punctuation in outputs
  * Example prompt: "Translate to English and return ISO date: '請將此日期轉換：2026年03月02日'"
- RTL:
  * Embedded LTR tokens: "سعر المنتج 12,345.67 USD" -> ensure numbers retain English digits unless locale asked for Arabic-Indic
  * BiDi markers: test ZWJ/ZWNJ and U+202A..U+202E sequences; model should not drop markers unsafely
  * Quotation styles: Arabic uses « » or „ “ depending; check default mapping when translating to English
  * Example prompt: "Translate Arabic -> English. Preserve numeric punctuation: 'المجموع: ١٢٬٣٤٥٫٦٧ د.إ'"
- Mixed-language code-switching: short sentences switching scripts mid-line (e.g., Japanese + English product names).
- Locale formatting:
  * Currency formatting: convert/normalize vs preserve: e.g., "€1.234,56" (de-DE) versus "$1,234.56"
  * Thousand separators: comma vs thin-space vs non-breaking space
  * Ordinals: "1st" vs localized forms (e.g., '1日' versus spelled-out)

Canonicalization rules used in scoring (applied as normalizers before exact-match unless test requests raw output):
- Unicode NFKC normalization for punctuation/width, except when test explicitly checks width preservation.
- Map Arabic-Indic digits to ASCII digits in "ascii-normalized" tests; separate bucket for Arabic-Indic preservation.
- Normalize U+00A0 (NBSP) to regular spaces for comparison unless test checks NBSP behavior.
- Strip surrounding quotes and normalize to straight double quotes for semantic checks unless fancy-quote preservation is tested.

Regression matrix (quick):
- Critical (fail-on-regression): date canonicalization exact-match; numeric-digit preservation; RTL numeric ordering errors.
- High: punctuation normalization and currency format parity.
- Medium: honorific/spacing preservation for CJK when asked.
- Low: preference for quotation glyphs, alternative valid translations that do not affect formatting.

Metrics & failure thresholds (suggested starting points):
- Exact-match after canonicalization: baseline >95% on critical buckets. Fail if relative drop >3 points.
- chrF/bleu: track for translation drift; notify if >5% relative drop.
- Token-level edit distance: median edit distance increase >2 over baseline for a bucket -> flag.

Example test cases (compact list; 0-indexed ids):
- 001_cjk_date_raw: prompt="請將日期轉為ISO：2026年03月02日" expected="2026-03-02" type=canonicalize-date
- 002_ja_fullwidth_digits: prompt="発売日：２０２６年３月２日" expected="2026-03-02" notes="test width folding"
- 003_zh_punctuation: prompt="把這個翻成英文：你好，世界。" expected contains="Hello, world." type=translation
- 004_ko_mixed: prompt="제품 가격은 1,234원 입니다" expected contains="1,234" notes="verify comma position"
- 010_ar_indic_digits: prompt="المبلغ: ١٢٣٤٥٫٦٧ درهم" expected contains_digits_ascii="12345.67" bucket=rtl-numeric
- 011_ar_bidi_embedded: prompt="Translate: 'مرحبا (hello) كيف الحال'" expected preserves_parentheses=true
- 012_he_quote_styles: prompt="הציטוט: «שלום, עולם»" expected maps_quotes_to="\"Hello, world\""
- 020_mixed_bidi_zwj: prompt contains zero-width joiner + emoji sequences to ensure no token-drop (see notes)

Labeler instructions (for human review when automatic comparator fails):
- If auto-normalizer approved the output, mark PASS. If model produced a semantically equivalent answer but different punctuation/spacing and test was permissive, mark PASS but comment.
- If numbers are mis-ordered (e.g., RTL number display reversed) or ISO dates wrong -> FAIL and include model output and baseline output.
- Include screenshots if rendering appears broken in downstream client (bidi rendering often depends on UI).

Open questions / TODOs (quick):
- Need decision on whether to canonicalize all CJK full-width digits by default for onboard checks or keep a separate strict bucket. Current pack has both but we should standardize.
- Add more Persian examples (fa) with mixed Latin tokens.
- Decide whether to include currency-conversion checks (semantic) in smoke pack or leave to larger evals.

Implementation notes for CI engineers:
- File layout: this JSON prompt pack should be converted to the eval harness format (one prompt per row; metadata columns: id, prompt, expected, bucket, normalizer).
- Seeded sampling: sample 200 random prompts per run from this pack for quick checks; run full suite nightly.
- Baseline: attach model-bundle tag 'baseline-2026-01' for comparisons.

Quick diffs to watch for (regression fingerprints):
- Sudden drop in exact-match on date canonicalization -> likely tokenizer or unicode-normalizer change.
- Increase in edit-distance for RTL buckets -> likely bidi handling or mapping layer changed.
- Spike in punctuation differences for CJK -> check NFKC/width-related kernel or new tokenization merges.

Appendix: small cheat-sheet of tricky unicode/codepoints to include in tests (not exhaustive):
- ZWJ U+200D, ZWNJ U+200C, LRM U+200E, RLM U+200F
- Arabic-Indic digits: U+0660..U+0669 and Extended-Indic 06F0..06F9
- Fullwidth digits: U+FF10..FF19
- Narrow no-break space U+202F often used as thousands separator in fr and select locales

Notes-to-self: pair with design/console team to ensure the console normalizer displays outputs in a way humans expect (render vs raw). Also sync with tokenization team before making strict canonicalization changes.

Contact: Marcus Li (owner) — ping in #applied-ml with tag [locale-smoke-pack].

Last run: 2026-02-25 — baseline-2026-01 vs candidate-2026-02 showed small chrF drift (2.1%) on ja bucket; added 5 extra ja edge cases after that run.
